prompts.label: Canonical midterm wording
prompts.text: A dairy farm in Eau Claire produces 1000 tons of waste manure and wants to get rid of it. The farmer is willing to give the manure away for free. A corn farmer in Menomonie is willing to pay 0.5 dollars per ton for manure and can take at most 500 tons. A soybean farmer in Black River Falls is willing to pay 1.5 dollars per ton and can take at most 500 tons. Transportation costs 0.1 dollars per ton from Eau Claire to Menomonie and 0.2 dollars per ton from Eau Claire to Black River Falls. Each transportation route has capacity 1000 tons. The cooperative maximizes total profit. What is the optimal manure allocation and can the dairy farmer get rid of all 1000 tons?

prompts.label: Paraphrased complete wording
prompts.text: Formulate the manure disposal network as a coordinated supply-chain problem. The Eau Claire dairy has up to 1000 tons of manure available at zero supply cost. Menomonie can receive no more than 500 tons and pays 0.5 dollars per ton. Black River Falls can receive no more than 500 tons and pays 1.5 dollars per ton. Shipping manure from Eau Claire costs 0.1 dollars per ton to Menomonie and 0.2 dollars per ton to Black River Falls. Each shipping route can carry at most 1000 tons. Maximize cooperative profit.
